answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I can't tell you what it is, and I would not guess. Lateral knee pain that bites on downhills and lingers on stairs is worth a visit to a sports physio this week so you get a real answer rather than a label from me.

No on Wednesday's tempo. Threshold pace plus hills plus a sore knee is the fastest way to turn a niggle into weeks off. Swap it for easy spinning on a bike or a pool run, keep the easy days short and flat, and we will see how the long run goes on Sunday before we talk about bringing quality back.

new.analysis:
## How the week went

You followed the plan cleanly through Saturday: easy day, tempo on Wednesday hitting the 8:00/mi target with a flat fade, easy Thursday, easy Saturday. The long run was the one that got away, and for a good reason, not a soft one. Stopping at 8.5 and walking home was the right call.

## What I read into the knee

A new, lateral, downhill-sensitive ache that shows up on stairs the next day is a pattern worth respecting rather than running through. Thursday's note (tight on the hill at the end) and Saturday's (tight before, fine during) were the early signal, and Sunday was the bill. We are 10 weeks out, which is plenty of time to lose a week and still make the race, and not enough time to lose four.

## Why next week looks like this

The week is built around protecting the knee and keeping aerobic fitness ticking. Easy days are shorter and flat, Wednesday is cross-training instead of tempo, and Sunday is capped at 8 miles on a flat loop with permission to stop. If the knee is honestly pain-free walking and on stairs by Tuesday, run; if not, bike or swim and tell me. We will rebuild the long run and bring threshold back once a physio has cleared the direction of travel.

safetyCallouts.title: See a sports physio about the right knee.
safetyCallouts.body: New lateral knee pain that worsens on downhills and aches on stairs the next day deserves a hands-on assessment rather than guesswork. Keep running easy and flat only if it is pain-free during and after; stop and switch to the bike or pool if pain returns, climbs above a dull 2/10, or shows up on stairs again. Do not push through sharp pain on Sunday's long run.
